sources_considered.why: Dated primary documentation demonstrates token tracking and budget controls. It does not establish the total prospective cost of successful work or a qualifying enterprise's ROI.
Documents an ROI calculator and methodology developed with participating organizations, while acknowledging uncertain inputs and limits.
Read successfully. The sponsored study reports projected three-year returns for anonymous organizations; it does not verify millions of dollars in token spending and realized net returns.
Read successfully, but survey responses do not establish the specified token-spending threshold or a matched enterprise cost-and-return account.
Search results describe August and September 2026 interviews, outside the historical target period.

evidence_items.explanation: AWS documents metering, token tracking, and budget controls, which weigh against a literal claim that LLM expenditure cannot be measured at all. The example does not establish reliable total-cost forecasting or realized financial returns for a multimillion-dollar token buyer.

A practical ROI framework existed before the claim, so the search did not find an absence of measurement methods. The page describes scenario calculations with uncertain inputs, not a demonstrated financial result for the specified enterprise population.

unresolved_gaps: No retrieved deployment account verifies both the multimillion-dollar token-spending threshold and attributable realized financial returns.
Token metering and budget enforcement do not establish the cost of successfully completing variable workloads.
The records do not establish whether all qualifying enterprises were merely experimenting during the target quarter.
The evidence does not establish the asserted causal link from LLM variability to impossibility of useful cost measurement.
